$comment: The one place the brand's colours are defined. They used to live independently in three files —
mobile/lib/core/theme.dart, admin-web/src/styles.css and landing-web/src/index.css — and had
already begun to diverge, so changing the brand meant three edits and hoping none was missed.
Run `node tools/generate-design-tokens.mjs` after editing; the generated files are committed so
no build step is needed, and CI checks that regenerating produces no diff.
500 is the brand colour and is not adjusted: it is for fills, where white sits on top of it.
As small text on a light surface it only reaches 3.4:1, so `text` below is the darkened
variant for that job — an active nav item, a link, a label.
Checked as text against the harder of the two light surfaces (#f5f5f7), because these are used
as small bold labels. danger was #d64545 at about 4.3:1; success and warning were also just
under 4.5:1, so all three were nudged darker. They always ship with an icon and words, never
colour alone, so they still read in greyscale and in forced-colors mode.
status.$commentDark: Lightened for a dark background: the light-mode values fall to roughly 3.4:1 there.

navy.$comment: Landing page only — the marketing surface sits on a dark navy rather than the app's greys.

darkNeutral.$comment: Admin panel dark mode. The mobile app derives its dark palette from Material 3 instead.
